title: Collections Desk Guide: Hardship Extension Limits on Retail Installment Contracts
content:
A hardship extension defers one or more installments of a contract under Retail Installment Contracts to the end of the contract under a signed extension agreement. The limits that apply turn on the contract's credit tier.

## Eligibility window and deferral limits

| Tier | Installments paid, at least | Days past due, at least | Days past due, at most | Installments deferred by one extension, at most | Installments deferred per rolling 12 months, at most | Installments deferred over the life, at most | Days since the previous extension's effective date, at least |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 6 Fresh Start | 6 | 1 | 44 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 180 |
| Tier 5 Rebuild | 6 | 1 | 44 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 180 |
| Tier 4 Standard | 6 | 1 | 59 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 180 |
| Tier 3 Advantage | 4 | 0 | 59 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 180 |
| Tier 2 Preferred | 4 | 0 | 59 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 120 |
| Tier 1 Select | 3 | 0 | 59 | 2 | 3 | 6 | 120 |

A minimum of 0 days past due allows a current account; a minimum of 1 requires the contract to be at least one day past due.

## Fee and signature terms

| Tier | Extension fee per agreement (USD) | First extension of the contract's life carries no fee | Days an agreement sent for signature stays open |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 6 Fresh Start | 35.00 | no | 10 |
| Tier 5 Rebuild | 35.00 | no | 10 |
| Tier 4 Standard | 30.00 | no | 10 |
| Tier 3 Advantage | 30.00 | no | 10 |
| Tier 2 Preferred | 25.00 | yes | 10 |
| Tier 1 Select | 25.00 | yes | 10 |

The signature period is in calendar days; an agreement not signed within it lapses.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical accounts)

- A current Tier 3 Advantage account (0 days past due) is inside that tier's window; a current Tier 4 Standard account is not, because Tier 4 Standard needs at least 1 day past due.
- A Tier 5 Rebuild account 50 days past due is beyond that tier's 44-day limit; a Tier 2 Preferred account 50 days past due is within its 59-day limit.
- A Tier 2 Preferred contract whose previous extension took effect 130 days ago meets that tier's 120-day spacing; a Tier 4 Standard contract with the same history does not meet its 180 days.
